\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{નફરત} (naphrat)}{નફરત (naphrat)}]{\gu{નફરત} (naphrat) — hatred}

\label{lesson:GU-C457-naphrat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for disregard, then the Gujarati for a knock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{નફરત}}
\textbf{\gu{નફરત}} — \emph{naphrat} — \textquotedblleft{}hatred\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મને} \gu{ખોટા} \gu{વચનથી} \gu{નફરત} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mane khoṭā vacanthī naphrat che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I hate empty promises.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{નફરત}} (\emph{naphrat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{nafra}, \textquotedblleft{}aversion, running away\textquotedblright{}, which reached Gujarati through Persian \emph{nafrat}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naphrat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naphrat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mane khoṭā vacanthī naphrat che.} — I hate empty promises.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for disregard, then the Gujarati for a knock, then say \emph{naphrat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{નફરત} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hatred\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ધિક્કારવું} (dhikkārvũ)}{ધિક્કારવું (dhikkārvũ)}]{\gu{ધિક્કારવું} (dhikkārvũ) — to despise}

\label{lesson:GU-C457-dhikkarvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a knock, then the Gujarati for hatred.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ધિક્કારવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ધિક્કારવું}} — \emph{dhikkārvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to despise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{બધા} \gu{સ્વાર્થી} \gu{માણસને} \gu{ધિક્કારે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badhā svārthī māṇasne dhikkāre che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone despises a selfish person.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{સ્વાર્થી} \gu{માણસને} \gu{ધિક્કાર્યો}, \emph{teṇe svārthī māṇasne dhikkāryo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ધિક્કારવું}} (\emph{dhikkārvũ}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{dhikkāra}, \textquotedblleft{}reproach\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{dhik}, \textquotedblleft{}fie!\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists the Gujarati verb (CDIAL 6808).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhikkārvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhikkārvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badhā svārthī māṇasne dhikkāre che.} — Everyone despises a selfish person.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a knock, then the Gujarati for hatred, then say \emph{dhikkārvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{તિરસ્કાર} (tiraskār)}{તિરસ્કાર (tiraskār)}]{\gu{તિરસ્કાર} (tiraskār) — contempt}

\label{lesson:GU-C457-tiraskar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for hatred, then the Gujarati for to despise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{તિરસ્કાર}}
\textbf{\gu{તિરસ્કાર}} — \emph{tiraskār} — \textquotedblleft{}contempt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તેની} \gu{આંખમાં} \gu{મારા} \gu{માટે} \gu{તિરસ્કાર} \gu{હતો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tenī ā̃khmā̃ mārā māṭe tiraskār hato.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was contempt for me in his eyes.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{તિરસ્કાર}} (\emph{tiraskār}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{tiraskāra}, which Monier-Williams gives as \textquotedblleft{}placing aside\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}abuse, censure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiraskār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tiraskār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tenī ā̃khmā̃ mārā māṭe tiraskār hato.} — There was contempt for me in his eyes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for hatred, then the Gujarati for to despise, then say \emph{tiraskār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અદેખાઈ} (adekhāī)}{અદેખાઈ (adekhāī)}]{\gu{અદેખાઈ} (adekhāī) — envy}

\label{lesson:GU-C457-adekhai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to despise, then the Gujarati for contempt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અદેખાઈ}}
\textbf{\gu{અદેખાઈ}} — \emph{adekhāī} — \textquotedblleft{}envy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મિત્રની} \gu{નવી} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{જોઈને} \gu{તેને} \gu{અદેખાઈ} \gu{થઈ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mitranī navī gāḍī joīne tene adekhāī thaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Seeing his friend's new car, he felt envious.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અદેખાઈ}} (\emph{adekhāī}) is built from the negative \emph{a-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, the stem of \emph{dekhvũ}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL traces to \emph{*dṛkṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}sees\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6507), and the noun ending \emph{-āī}: probably the feeling of not bearing to see another's good.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adekhāī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adekhāī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mitranī navī gāḍī joīne tene adekhāī thaī.} — Seeing his friend's new car, he felt envious.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to despise, then the Gujarati for contempt, then say \emph{adekhāī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{અદેખાઈ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Envy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અણગમો} (aṇgamo)}{અણગમો (aṇgamo)}]{\gu{અણગમો} (aṇgamo) — dislike}

\label{lesson:GU-C457-angamo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for contempt, then the Gujarati for envy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અણગમો}}
\textbf{\gu{અણગમો}} — \emph{aṇgamo} — \textquotedblleft{}dislike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મીરાને} \gu{ભીડ} \gu{માટે} \gu{અણગમો} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mīrāne bhīḍ māṭe aṇgamo che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mira dislikes crowds.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અણગમો}} (\emph{aṇgamo}) is built from the negative \emph{aṇ-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, and the stem of \textbf{\gu{ગમવું}} (\emph{gamvũ}), \textquotedblleft{}to like\textquotedblright{}, with the noun ending \emph{-o}: a not-liking. CDIAL lists the verb, \textquotedblleft{}to approve\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{gamyatē}, \textquotedblleft{}one goes, it is understood\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4033).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṇgamo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṇgamo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Mīrāne bhīḍ māṭe aṇgamo che.} — Mira dislikes crowds.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for contempt, then the Gujarati for envy, then say \emph{aṇgamo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{અણગમો} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dislike\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
